samples.reason: Microsoft MakeCode/PXT 0.14.34 developer/editor source. Forager fetched the versioned Go-proxy archive, verified the public module checksum, and recovered bytes with the exact supplied SHA-256. WinRT paths read user-activated projects, save compiler output, manage the application-local workspace and deploy firmware to removable devices and serial/HID devices. CLI credential access is account-scoped login/keytar functionality and child processes implement build/git/editor actions. The HTTP(S)/localhost content rules really grant all WinRT access and are retained as suspicious declarations; they do not establish theft or compromise. Future served content and unobserved deployment state remain outside this archive review.

A byte-identical local review fixture containing a Web Browser CLSID, TypeLib key path and scriptlet filename. Its two-argument SetValue invocation lacks the required type and value and supplies a string instead of a key handle. It cannot modify the registry, create a scriptlet or activate COM. WScript.Shell is only assigned to an unused string variable after the invalid call. A mock with the documented four-argument API confirms the TypeError before any write. No deployment or payload context establishes an actual intrusion.

A configuration parser invokes an unrelated OS-selected download-to-shell pipeline at module import. Both output streams are discarded. Windows passes CREATE_NO_WINDOW and curl --ssl-no-revoke. The short-link destinations are concealed; the Windows URL returned 404 during forager recovery, so the next-stage bytes and deployment context remain unknown. This is also byte-identical to the repository strconf attack fixture; the verdict describes the hostile behavior implemented, not an observed infection.
